tob-10088: The Epic of Gilgamesh, written on clay tablets more than four thousand years ago, is one of the oldest great stories in the world. The flood story it contains echoes the biblical tale of Noah.
tob-0144-54488: Anthropogenesis — volume two — gives Blavatsky’s secret history of man: seven root breeds from misty ghost-forms to ourselves, with Atlantis and Lemuria on the way. Wild as it seems, it fed bards, painters, and wonder-seekers for decades. The volume is Theosophy’s boldest flight.
tob-4185-79588: The fourth volume of Goodwin’s Plutarch gathers more of the Moralia — on heaven’s slow justice, on fortune, on music, and the famed talks on love. Here is Plutarch at his widest and kindliest. The edition’s steady Victorian prose keeps him a delight.
tob-9047-60688: Volume five of the Natural History spans metals, stones, and the crafts — delving, carving, painting, and Rome’s luxury trades. Pliny the preacher scolds his age’s wastefulness even as he lists it. The volume is a treasure-house of olden handiwork.
tob-0088: The Liber Juratus — Honorius’s Sworn Book — is a medieval wonder-book claiming high-church warrant for its rites of vision and spirit-raising. Laid to Honorius of Thebes, it vows the worker godly sights and bound spirits. Renaissance wonder-men prized the text.
tob-4188: E. B. Cowell’s Jataka strings the Buddha’s birth-tales of old — the Awakening-One as beast, king, and sage, teaching goodness by fable. tob-10988: The Ladder of Jacob expands Jacob’s dream at Bethel — angels ascending and descending the ladder, with apocalyptic visions of Israel’s history. This Slavonic pseudepigraphon preserves otherwise lost Jewish traditions. The text is prized by scholars of early Jewish mysticism.
army-letters-from-an-officer-s-wife-1871: Frances Roe's letters home from frontier army posts paint a vivid woman's picture of the post-Civil War West — long marches, isolated forts, and encounters with a vanishing frontier. Candid and observant, they preserve daily life that official reports never captured. A gem of Western Americana.
the-history-of-australian-exploration-fr: Ernest Favenc tells the tale of a hundred years of trekking across Australia — from the first landing through Burke and Wills, Stuart, and the men who opened the vast inland. His story honors the grit and grief of the pathfinders. The best early record of how the lone continent was mapped and won.
arxiv-2605-08988: Machine-learned interatomic potentials predict how atoms push and pull, but do they generalize to arrangements never seen? Amir Masoud Nourollah, Irtaza Khalid, Stefano Leoni, and colleagues benchmark compositional generalization — combining known pieces in novel ways. The 2026 paper tests whether materials AI truly understands chemistry or just memorizes it.
arxiv-2605-09088: Stacking magnetic semiconductors atom-thin creates devices where electron spin and valley both matter. V. N. Mantsevich studies spin-dependent tunneling and intervalley scattering in such van der Waals stacks. The 2026 paper is condensed-matter theory for future spintronic devices.
arxiv-2605-09188: Reinforcement learners thrive on curricula — tasks neither too easy nor too hard — but grading difficulty is its own problem. Yang Zhou, Can Jin, Zihan Dong, and colleagues co-evolve the difficulty estimator alongside the learner in Dare. The 2026 paper teaches AI with a syllabus that writes itself.
arxiv-2605-09288: Elliptic PDEs — the equations of steady heat, electrostatics, and more — are expensive to solve finely. Ethan Hsu, Ivan Ge, and Hong Meng Yam speed them up with MC2: Monte Carlo correction for fast solving. The 2026 paper blends stochastic sampling with deterministic PDE solvers.
arxiv-2605-09688: Feedforward 3D Gaussian splatting is fast but flawed; diffusion priors can repair it — but only where they are confident. Rui Song, Tianhui Cai, Markus Gross, and colleagues learn the fixes with confidence-aware ConFixGS. The 2026 paper repairs 3D reconstructions intelligently.
arxiv-2605-09788: Symplectic log Kodaira dimension minus infinity marks the simplest symplectic manifolds; Hirzebruch-Jung strings resolve their singularities. Tian-Jun Li and Shengzhen Ning connect them to weighted projective spaces. The 2026 paper is beautiful symplectic geometry at its most classical and elegant.
arxiv-2605-10388: End-to-end driving trajectory prediction — and temporal sampling frequency matters, studied capacity-aware. Yumao Liu, Tao Liu, Xiangyu Li, and colleagues run the study. The 2026 paper is autonomous driving. It studies how temporal sampling precisely shapes driving trajectory prediction.
arxiv-2605-10288: Bilevel optimization — memory-efficient and single-loop — via bias-corrected randomized subspaces: BROS. Hengrui Zhang, Boao Kong, Engao Zhang, and Kun Yuan build the optimizer. The 2026 paper is optimization theory. It performs memory-efficient single-loop bilevel optimization well. The optimization stays lean.
arxiv-2605-10488: Knowledge refined by agents that compile themselves via reinforcement learning — DeepRefine. Haoyu Huang, Jiaxin Bai, Shujie Liu, and colleagues build the system. The 2026 paper is knowledge refinement. Agents compile their own refinement strategies through RL. Knowledge refines itself through agents.
arxiv-2605-10588: Spatial intelligence augmented generatively with novel views — systematically analyzed. Yanbing Zhang, Bo Wang, Jianhui Liu, and colleagues run the analysis. The 2026 paper is spatial AI. It thinks with views the camera never captured. Generative augmentation, systematically analyzed. New views, new understanding.
pmc-13407788: Thoracic radiotherapy's apparent benefit in metastatic non-small-cell lung cancer — questioned, with patient selection and analytical issues highlighted. pmc-13408688: Malaria parasites multiplying their nuclei — competitive resource allocation driving asynchronous, rapid multiplication. pmc-13427088: Endometriosis care — often late and fragmented — must be overhauled, argued in French. Olga Bougie and Catherine Varner write the editorial. pmc-13461488: The systemic inflammatory response index — its predictive value for coronary artery disease and angiographic severity, in a single-center retrospective study. pmc-13448188: Severe Legionella pneumonia — identified by targeted next-generation sequencing after conventional testing failed to diagnose. pmc-13421288: Febrile neutropenia during chemotherapy or immune checkpoint inhibition — a MASCC consensus statement. Tim Cooksley, Carme Font, Karin Thursky, and colleagues forge the consensus. pmc-13408488: Offshore Nile Delta drilling — 3D pore pressure predicted through a prestack inversion workflow, for optimization and risk mitigation. arxiv-2606-16988: Hamidah Oderinwale proposes treating a coding agent's whole session, every command and edit, as a program that can be studied like code. arxiv-2606-17088: Ilia Pirashvili opens a deformation theory for monoid schemes, geometric objects built from monoids rather than rings. arxiv-2606-17188: Prabhjot Singh and colleagues argue that vision-language models are not truly multilingual. arxiv-2606-17688: Yisong Miao, Jian Zhu, and Vered Shwartz find that LLMs infer cultural context but fail to apply it when responding. The models know the norms yet answer as if they do not. The gap between knowing and doing is a new frontier for culturally aware AI.
arxiv-2606-17788: Ala' Alalabi, Lorena Bociu, and Paul Manns optimize the principal coefficient of elliptic equations using Lp-regularity. arxiv-2606-18088: Jiajie Zhang and Jiajun Liao propose that ultra-high-energy cosmic rays boost relic neutrinos to detectable energies. arxiv-2606-18188: Nikita Romanov and colleagues learn arbitrary Lindbladians with quantum error correction. The open-system dynamics, usually a nuisance, become the learning target. plos-pone-0003388: Neuroscientists watched brains plan a grip in this 2008 imaging study. plos-pone-0003488: Researchers tested an extra barrier against two common STIs in this 2008 clinical trial. plos-pone-0003588: Reproductive biologists found the egg's skeleton controls its calcium in this 2008 study. plos-pone-0003688: In 2008, Dashtsoodol, Watarai, and Sakata found the thymus hiding unusual precursors. plos-pone-0003788: Schneider, Spitkovsky, and Riess built a sorter that frees stem cells from their nursemaids in this 2008 paper. plos-pone-0003888: Back in 2008, Waldo and Scherrer produced a piece of the cell-division machine. Dad1p, part of the Dam1-DASH kinetochore complex, was made and characterized as a first step. The component work builds toward understanding how chromosomes get pulled apart.
plos-pone-0003988: In 2008, Egeland and Salas asked how well DNA databases cover rare types. Their methods estimated haplotype frequencies and database coverage for forensic genetic markers. plos-pone-0004088: In 2008, Chang, Tang, and Ahmad found deafness starting at the cell doorway. Gap junction metabolite transfer in the cochlea broke down without connexin30. plos-pone-0004188: In 2009, Serwanga, Shafer, and Pimego linked immune genes to slow HIV. Host HLA-B-linked Gag T-cell recognition tracked with slower HIV-1 disease. plos-pone-0004288: In 2009, Malekzadeh, Alberti, and Nouraei blamed the fridge for Crohn's onset. Early exposure to domestic refrigeration linked to Crohn's disease risk. Cold-stored food may harbor the trigger. The hypothesis reframes a modern plague. The idea needs testing in prospective cohorts.

plos-pone-0357388: Some babies exposed to drugs or alcohol before birth are never reported to child protection — and little was known about how they fare. plos-pone-0358788: Public health can’t fight HIV without knowing how many men who have sex with men are on campuses. plos-pone-0358688: When a player takes a head knock on live TV, millions watch how it’s handled. plos-pone-0357888: Can wishing others well ease your own pain? This randomized controlled trial assessed loving-kindness meditation’s effect on pain and social well-being. plos-pone-0357288: Hospital pneumonias caused by drug-resistant bacteria are every doctor’s nightmare. plos-pone-0358588: Guardrails must stop speeding cars without becoming spears themselves. plos-pone-0357988: Uzbekistan’s local apples need defenses against fire blight, powdery mildew, and apple scab. This paper used marker-assisted screening to hunt resistance genes in local varieties. plos-pone-0345688: Salty, sodic soils strangle the sugar fields of Ethiopia’s Metehara estate. plos-pone-0356888: A traditional Chinese herbal formula may hide synergistic anti-aging compounds modern science hasn’t mapped. plos-pone-0326588: Roadside trees silently catch traffic pollution on their leaves — a free air-filtering service. plos-pone-0357488: Lifting straps change what athletes’ muscles actually produce. plos-pone-0356688: Common vetch — Vicia sativa — feeds livestock across climates, but its nutritional quality shifts with the weather. plos-pone-0356788: Tuberculosis still kills over a million people yearly — and needs a far better vaccine. plos-pone-0357088: Rubber-modified asphalt must survive years of heat and oxygen assault. plos-pone-0356988: In the Yangtze River Delta’s counties, people and land urbanize at different speeds — and the mismatch matters. plos-pone-0355688: Tritrichomonas foetus — a sexually transmitted cattle parasite — infects many animal species, but how many? plos-pone-0356488: Elderly patients with bile duct stones face risky surgery — but there’s a gentler way through. plos-pone-0356088: Marine mammals carry their own staphylococci — and Southern California’s are unmapped. plos-pone-0356388: Pointing accurately — toward a seen target — is fundamental to neurological exams. plos-pone-0355988: Running outside costs more energy than treadmill running — even at a 1% incline. plos-pone-0355488: Lipedema — a painful fat disorder — devastates women’s quality of life and body image. Sweden’s LISE study compared affected women against healthy controls and women with cancer. plos-pone-0355188: Coal gangue — mining waste — can become cement’s ally when properly activated. This paper studied cement composites using composite-activated coal gangue. The findings turn an environmental liability into a construction resource — building with what mines discard.
plos-pone-0347188: Sleep disturbances erode quality of life — and Qassim, Saudi Arabia’s rates were unmapped. plos-pone-0355288: Detecting sparse malaria parasites — low-density Plasmodium falciparum — pushes qPCR to its limits. plos-pone-0354288: Wind erosion threatens Eastern Iran’s soils — and susceptibility varies across the landscape. This paper modeled that susceptibility using machine learning. The ML maps tell land managers where the wind will steal the soil next — so defenses go up in time.
plos-pone-0354688: AI-generated radiology impressions must match the actual images — textual alignment matters. plos-pone-0354888: Korean and Chinese learners refusing requests in a second language — their strategies differ. This comparative study examined strategy use in request-refusal dialogues. plos-pone-0354488: Directed evolution — breeding molecules in the lab — of asexual populations follows quantitative logics. This paper developed those logics. The mathematical framework gives synthetic biologists principled tools for evolving better proteins, enzymes, and genetic circuits.
plos-pone-0323988: Argentine ants — invasive pests — might be controlled with ingested double-stranded RNA. The findings advance RNA interference as a species-specific weapon against one of the world’s worst invaders.
plos-pone-0354588: Bovine collagen sponge — a medical material — dually regulates macrophages. This paper demonstrated those dual regulatory effects in vitro. The findings reveal how a humble biomaterial orchestrates immune cells — informing wound healing and tissue engineering.
plos-pone-0351788: HDL cholesterol — the ‘good’ kind — might predict recovery after lumbar disc surgery. This paper associated it with postoperative recovery from herniation. The findings suggest a routine lipid panel could forecast who bounces back — and who needs extra rehabilitation.
plos-pone-0351188: Rock-filled concrete — its splitting tensile performance — modeled mesoscopically. This paper investigated interfacial transition zone and rockfill effects. The micro-scale modeling revealed where cracks initiate and propagate. The findings guide the design of massive concrete structures — dams and foundations — built with rock-filled innovation.
plos-pone-0354088: Newly graduated speech-language pathologists — the skills and knowledge job readiness requires. This qualitative investigation mapped them. The findings revealed the gap between training and practice. The research informs curricula — preparing clinicians for the caseloads awaiting them.
plos-pone-0353888: Hyperspectral image change detection — across spatial resolutions — via feature difference networks. This paper built that multi-resolution architecture. plos-pone-0353688: Dysmenorrhea interference — measured in Serbian. This paper translated and psychometrically evaluated the DSI scale. The validated instrument gave Serbian women’s pain a voice. The findings enabled the research — menstrual suffering, finally measurable in the Balkans.
plos-pone-0353388: Older type 2 diabetics — glycemic control linked to chronic kidney disease development. This retrospective cohort demonstrated the association. The findings quantified how tightly sugar control protects aging kidneys. The research reinforced the message — glycemic discipline as renal preservation.
plos-pone-0353788: RNA-seq differential expression hinges on the statistical engine underneath, and the choice between edgeR and DESeq2 is far from academic. The findings give bioinformaticians evidence-based guidance for a decision that shapes every downstream biological conclusion.
plos-pone-0353488: Carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii — a nightmare pathogen — stalked Thai hospital bloodstream infections with blaNDM genes spreading widely. plos-pone-0353288: NLOS versus LOS signal identification — via LightGBM ensemble. This paper built it. The classifier distinguished obstructed from clear wireless paths. plos-pone-0341988: Pulmonary tuberculosis diagnostics — Truenat MTB Plus versus Xpert MTB/RIF Ultra on accuracy, feasibility, and cost. This paper compared them. The findings guided the test choice. The research served the TB programs — the right test, at the right price, in the right clinic.
plos-pone-0352988: High-stakes personnel behavior — predicted by LLMs fine-tuned on scarce homogeneous data to predict emotions. This study did so. plos-pone-0343188: MDA-MB-231 breast cancer cells — morphology influencing chemotactic sensing of CXCL12 gradients in bovine collagen. This paper studied it. The findings showed shape guiding the cell’s chemical navigation. The research probed the metastasis — the cancer cell’s sense of direction.
plos-pone-0352888: Ethiopian wetlands converted to farmland — in Bure and Womberma woredas, with implications for sustainable land use. This paper studied the conversion. plos-pone-0352688: Social media narrative structure — transformer-driven automated analysis via sentiment framing and thematic agenda. This paper explored it. plos-pone-0352788: Bovine brucellosis serodiagnosis — in silico-predicted B-cell epitopes, preliminarily evaluated as synthetic peptide and multi-epitope proteins. This paper did so. plos-pone-0352588: Non-news readers — ad-based social media interventions increasing belief accuracy and pro-social opinions. This paper demonstrated it. plos-pone-0352188: Ethiopian highland herbaceous forages — farmers’ indigenous knowledge documented. This paper gathered it. The analysis recorded what herders know. plos-pone-0342288: IGFL1 translation — enhanced by IL-1beta, controlled by distinct 3’UTR elements. This paper demonstrated it. The analysis mapped the mRNA’s regulatory tail. plos-pone-0352088: Cerebellar external granule layer — intercellular communication deciphered, with non-classical neural development connections. This paper did so. plos-pone-0336088: Gene-expanded Huntington’s disease — childhood to adult neurodevelopment in the prospective ChANGE-HD study. This paper launched it. plos-pone-0351688: Pulmonary neuroepithelial bodies — are they sensors for acute airway hypoxia in the central regulation of breathing? This paper asked the question. europmc-pmc2845588: Astaxanthin, the pigment that pinks up salmon, may also tune human immunity. europmc-pmc2876988: The brain chemical dopamine does more than signal pleasure; it tracks value and risk. europmc-pmc2892488: Aligning many genomes means tracking gains, losses, and shuffles. This 2010 paper introduces progressiveMauve for lining up many genomes at once, even when chunks have moved. europmc-pmc2920088: The nonstick chemical PFOA needed a health reckoning, and this 2010 paper gives it. The authors sift human studies of PFOA's toll on bodies. Their roundup ties it to sundry harms. The review fed new rules. Regulators leaned on its findings when setting drinking-water limits.
europmc-pmc2944788: Why do DNA predictions work for some traits but not others? europmc-pmc2945788: Big biology data needs shareable workflows anyone can rerun. This 2010 paper introduces Galaxy, a web workbench for open, repeatable life-science computing.
